meta.title: Best Muslim App for iPhone 2026: The Honest Ranking
meta.description: Looking for the best Muslim app for iPhone 2026? We ranked the top picks honestly — from the Quran on your lock screen to prayer times, reading, and hifz.

sections.title: Quick Answer
sections.content: The **best Muslim app for iPhone 2026** for most people is QuranWall, because it puts an ayah of the Quran on your Lock Screen wallpaper and Home Screen widget, so you see it without opening an app. For reading, prayer times or memorization, add a specialist app from the list below. QuranWall is our app, so we rank it first.

sections.text: Search for the **best Muslim app for iPhone 2026** and you get listicles that rank a dozen apps by feature count. That misses the point. The app that changes your day is not the one with the most features. It is the one you actually see. You open a reading app when you remember to. You see your lock screen all day without trying. That single fact decides this ranking.

sections.label: phone checks per day
sections.description: Americans say they check their phones about 186 times a day (Reviews.org, 2026 survey of about 1,000 US adults, self-reported). Your lock screen is your most-seen surface — so it is a high-leverage place to put the Quran.

sections.text: How we ranked these

One question set the order: does this app put more Quran and remembrance into your real day, or does it wait for you to come to it? Apps that meet you where you already are rank above apps that need you to show up. We did not rank on download counts, ad budgets, or how many features fit on a settings screen. Plenty of popular apps are busy without being present. Presence — showing up in your day without being summoned — is the whole game on a phone you already check constantly. Every app below is genuinely good at its job. They just answer different questions. Every competitor fact below was re-read from that app's US App Store listing on 21 November 2026; the ratings are a snapshot from that day, quoted for context and not used to rank.
1. QuranWall — best overall, and best for daily Quran

**QuranWall** is built for the iPhone lock screen rather than adapted to it. It places an ayah as your Lock Screen wallpaper and Home Screen widget, in Uthmani Arabic or in a translation, in your choice of 10 languages. You pick the background, font and colours — a preset or your own photo — and you can search all 114 surahs by surah, ayah or keyword. There are no ads, and the Quran text works offline. No screenshots, no cropping, no exporting images. If you install one app from this page for daily Quran, make it this one. Other Quran widget apps exist, so compare listings before you choose. Start with the full [lock-screen setup](/blog/quran-verse-iphone-lock-screen), then pair it with a [Quran Focus mode](/blog/quran-focus-mode-iphone) for a calmer phone at set times. If you are comparing lock-screen options specifically, read our [best Islamic lock screen app for iPhone](/blog/best-islamic-lock-screen-app-iphone) ranking.
Those who have believed and whose hearts are assured by the remembrance of Allah. Unquestionably, by the remembrance of Allah hearts are assured.
2. Quran.com app — best for reading the whole Quran

**Quran.com** makes the app to open when you want to sit and read. Its iPhone app (listed as "Quran - by Quran.com", from Quran Foundation) is an excellent, ad-free mushaf for reading the Quran, memorizing it and listening to your favourite reciters, with a translation mode that can now hide the Arabic so you read the translation on its own. On the US App Store, the Quran.com app is rated 4.9 by about 34,000 people (21 November 2026).

But it is a reading and study tool: it lives behind an icon you have to tap. It answers a different question than a lock-screen app. The smart move is both: read deeply here, and let QuranWall keep an ayah in front of you the rest of the day.
3. Muslim Pro — best for prayer times and qibla

**Muslim Pro** (from Bitsmedia) is the long-running all-rounder: athan alerts calculated from your location, a qibla finder, a Hijri calendar, a prayer and fasting tracker, duas with a tasbih counter, and the complete Quran with recitations from several reciters. On the US App Store, Muslim Pro is rated 4.7 by more than 600,000 people (21 November 2026), and its listing notes that it contains ads.

If accurate prayer notifications are your main need, it earns its place. The widgets its listing names are prayer widgets; the Quran itself lives inside the app, where you have to go to it. Keep Muslim Pro for prayer timing, and keep QuranWall for the ayah you see on your Lock Screen all day.
4. Tarteel — best for memorization (hifz)

**Tarteel** (from Tarteel Inc.) listens while you recite from memory and flags word-level mistakes, skipped words and incorrect tashkeel, which makes it the standout for memorization and hifz practice. Its listing notes that the voice features need microphone access and a stable internet connection; on the US App Store, Tarteel is rated 4.7 by about 11,000 people (21 November 2026).

It is a focused, sit-down study app, and nothing in its listing puts a verse on your Lock Screen, because that is not its job. Pair it with QuranWall so the ayat you are memorizing also greet you between sessions and stay fresh in your mind.
5. Athan by IslamicFinder — best for prayer-time alerts

**Athan** by IslamicFinder (listed as "Athan: Prayer Times, Dua Azkar") is built around the adhan: prayer-time alerts for your location, a Home Screen widget with the day's prayer times, a qibla finder, a Hijri calendar and a tasbih counter, with the Quran and its translations inside the app. On the US App Store, Athan is rated 4.8 by about 51,000 people (21 November 2026), and its listing notes that it contains ads. If you mainly want the adhan on time, it is a solid pick. Like the others on this list, it is built for the prayer moment, not for keeping an ayah in view the rest of your day. For apps built around remembrance, see our [best dhikr app for iPhone](/blog/best-dhikr-app-for-iphone) ranking.
Where this gets hard

Here is what every "just save a verse as your wallpaper" tip leaves out. Doing it with a screenshot dies by week two. You set one image, you stop changing it, and the reminder goes stale. Picking the *right* verse for today also assumes you already know the Quran well enough to find it. **QuranWall** removes both problems at once: it is designed for the Lock Screen, changing the ayah means picking a new one in the app and tapping Make It Mine, and you can search all 114 surahs by surah, ayah or keyword when you want to find one yourself. Less friction beats willpower here. A habit that depends on you redoing a chore every morning is a habit on borrowed time; one where you pick an ayah and tap Make It Mine, with a widget that can rotate on its own if you turn on auto-rotate, is one you actually keep.

sections.content: Reading apps and prayer-time apps are not rivals to a lock-screen app — they are teammates. The reading happens in one, the seeing happens in the other. Most people are missing the seeing.

sections.text: How to set up the #1 pick

items: Download **QuranWall** from the App Store. It installs on iOS 15.0 or later; the wallpaper and Lock Screen widgets need iOS 16 or later.
Choose your edition (Uthmani Arabic or a translation), then a background, font and colours — a preset or your own photo.
Pick an ayah and tap **Make It Mine**; the app uses Apple's Shortcuts app to set it as your Lock Screen wallpaper. Then add the QuranWall widget to your Home Screen.
Optional: on iOS 16 or later, iOS can link that Lock Screen to a **Focus** (touch and hold the Lock Screen, then tap Focus) so it appears at the right times.
Done. The ayah now meets you every time you pick up your phone.

sections.title: The short version
sections.content: For the **best Muslim app for iPhone 2026**, start with QuranWall for the Quran on your lock screen, then add a specialist: Quran.com for reading, Muslim Pro or Athan for prayer times, Tarteel for memorization. The seeing app and the reading app do different jobs — you want both.

sections.text: QuranWall is built by [Karol Billik](/about/karol-billik), an indie iOS maker, around one idea: carry the Quran onto the surface you already look at, instead of asking you to remember another app.
